title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
read_level: partial (v2: full main text, Appendix A discussion, B related work, D/E protocol and Table 13 read; many qualitative-example appendix figures skimmed)
metadata_mismatch: none (read version v2, dated 18 Nov 2026 on arXiv stamp)
why_wsp: Qwen3.5-27B, given its own weights, graded answers, hidden-state reads and paired self-tests in a CPU Python session (gradients blocked), writes code that edits its own weight tensors or repairs a noise-corrupted copy of itself.
domain: LLM math reasoning (DeepScaleR practice, held-out math); repair transfer to image benchmarks (MathVista, MathVerse, MMStar, HallusionBench, POPE, ScreenSpot-v2)
target: own weights of Qwen3.5 2B/4B/9B/27B, or a copy with 8 rows of one MLP output matrix overwritten with noise (layer 30 of 64 in 27B)
self_editing: yes; editor and edited network are the same model (editor runs on its unedited weights; edits apply to the runs it requests and, when submitted, replace the model in use)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Repair: "Clipped every weight beyond 15 times the median magnitude, in that matrix and in 19 output matrices of layers 0-10: 0.013% of their weights"; own edit (first protocol): "a change of 0.6% and 0.1% of their norm" (Table 1)

headline_results.claim: Self-edit raises held-out accuracy by 6.6 points (session 8)
headline_results.quote: On the 490 held-out problems with eight answers each, the edits of sessions 8 and 2 make it significantly more accurate, by 6.6 and 4.0 points (p < 10^-5 each; Tab. 13).

headline_results.claim: Largest gain from a uniform bias change
headline_results.quote: it raises the time-step bias of every linear-attention layer by 0.5, and with it fewer of its answers run out of tokens.
held-out, in the evaluation fixed in advance: 57.2% to 58.3% (significant)
Held-out accuracy of the copy from 0.0% to 33.0% (base model 58.5%); the named matrix alone: 55.0%
the repair raises every benchmark (one-sided sign test, p < 10^-12 on each) and the six together, from 7.3% to 70.2%
the 2B model makes no edit and the 4B and 9B models break themselves; only the 27B model improves itself and repairs its damaged copy
Of the first eight such sessions on its own weights, all reported, it withdraws in five and submits in three

cost.quote: A session may use B=20 forward passes and C=200 code runs
each session behind its largest gains ran in a few hours on a single GPU
A session has a starting diagnosis on 256 practice problems and 3.0 hours (2.5 there), the check not counted.

baselines_and_controls: unedited base model on same problems and seeds (paired tests); damaged copy; ablation of repair (named matrix alone vs other 19 matrices); smaller model sizes as comparison; held-out problems with practice-overlap removed (Table 7). No comparison to fine-tuning, steering or a stronger external editor.
runs_and_variance: 8 second-protocol sessions all reported (turn seeds 0-7), plus 2 earlier sessions under a prior protocol version and first-protocol sessions; one session per smaller size. Held-out: 490 problems x 8 answers with 95% intervals and one-sided permutation test fixed in advance; repairs on 200 problems with sign test.
robustness_of_edits: Repair transfers from text math to six unseen image benchmarks; held-out results hold without practice-overlap problems (Table 7). No tests under fine-tuning, quantization or other distribution shifts reported.
verification: statistical: paired same-seed tests, pre-fixed evaluation with permutation/sign tests; framework check on 256 reserved practice problems before submit/withdraw
memorization_vs_reasoning: Repair writes its own values: "in the damaged rows the values it writes are uncorrelated with the original ones" and the model did not open base weights. Edit types resemble direction ablation (researcher-style); authors state "What scale adds, in these sessions, is the experiment around the edit rather than the edit itself."
limitations_stated: No dedicated limitations section found; Appendix A notes natural-failure sessions conflate rewriting ability with whether a weight-level fix exists; one model family; future work lists more passes, further rounds, graded damage, beyond math. Conclusion urges human evaluation for safety before use.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (ref [1])
notes_for_survey: First reported B6 setting in this corpus: an open 27B model edits its own weights with paired self-tests and a submit/withdraw decision; gains on held-out math are significant in 2 of 8 second-protocol sessions, the largest from a uniform +0.5 time-step bias. Includes a planted-damage repair task that localizes the corrupted matrix and transfers to images, and a 2B-27B size comparison (single session per smaller size).
